notes: Cross-language contract for the desktop VM core (apps/builder-mac FlagshipBuilderCore/VM <-> apps/builder-windows src/VM <-> apps/builder-linux vm). Both test suites MUST consume this file so the cores cannot drift — the same role engine/golden/preseed-vectors.json plays for the preseed engine. States: created | installing | installed | awaitingPhoneUnlock | running | stopped | failed:install | failed:run. Events: startInstall | installSucceeded | installFailed | powerOn | guestUnlocked | powerOff | runtimeFailed. Effects: attachInstallerISO | detachInstallerISO | startVirtualMachine | stopVirtualMachine. 'sealed' mirrors VMConfig.awaitsPhoneUnlockAtBoot; transitions listing no 'sealed' key must hold for BOTH values.

installVerdict.notes: A hypervisor-level clean guest-stop during install is ambiguous (success poweroff / completed-install reboot / never-booted all look identical), so the verdict is duration-gated: elapsed >= minPlausibleInstallSeconds => installSucceeded, else installFailed with an actionable reason. Edge: exactly the minimum counts as success. Verdict tokens pin the EVENT chosen, not the failure prose (messages are per-platform).

resourcePlan.notes: gib = 2^30. Constants: default 6 GiB (4 GiB on hosts with at most 16 GiB RAM), floor 4 GiB, host reserve 4 GiB, absolute max 8 VMs, default main disk 64 GiB.

diskDurability.notes: How every hosted server's writable main disk is attached. Two VMs were left with zeroed system files by guest writes the host never flushed. Virtualization.framework (Mac): host-cached, every guest flush reaches the disk. QEMU (Windows, Linux): writeback cache with guest flushes honoured (never cache=unsafe or cache.no-flush), thread-pool I/O (works on every filesystem and on Windows, unlike O_DIRECT), and guest TRIM freeing space in the host image. Each QEMU port asserts every key=value below on the main -drive.

serverHealth.notes: A hosted server's own health report, read from .com by the order serial that created it (GET /api/order/<serial>/health, control-plane serverHealth.ts). 'response' is the raw body; each port reads it for serverDomain and renders the verdict at nowMs. null = nothing to show (another server, no report yet, malformed). Copy matches the phone apps (BoxHealth.verdict on iOS).

applianceSeed.notes: The one-use specialization seed a new hosted server reads (packages/flagship-builder appliance.ts encodeApplianceSeed is the reference; the guest specializer checks the header's length and body SHA-256 before decoding). The seed is sizeBytes long: the 80-byte ASCII header, the compact JSON body (keys in this order, no escaped '/'), then zeros. Node and Windows reproduce 'body' byte for byte; the Mac's JSONEncoder writes an equivalent body the guest accepts the same way.

nameValidation.notes: Bundle names are server FQDNs. Allowed: lowercase a-z, 0-9, '.', '-'; non-empty; not '.' or '..'; no LEADING dot; no TRAILING dot (the trailing-dot rejection is one deliberate tightening over the original Mac validate() — Win32 silently strips trailing dots and no real FQDN ends in one; the Mac side should adopt it).

bootEvidence.notes: Studio decides a sealed guest has unlocked ONLY from the box's own signed health report on .com, never by fetching https://<server domain>/ from the host: the name does not exist until the box registers it, and a lookup before then is cached as NXDOMAIN by home routers for the zone's negative TTL (30 min seen on Windows 2026-10-18), leaving Studio on 'Waiting for you to unlock' on a healthy box. provesBoxIsUp = the daemon is active, the relay tunnel is up, the report was received after this boot began (receivedAtMs >= poweredOnAtMs), the guest's uptime fits inside the time since this boot began (+60 s slack, so a previous boot's report is never taken), and it is under 5 minutes old at nowMs. A server without an order serial has no health report and falls back to probing its name.

awaitingUnlockCopy.notes: The sidebar/detail copy while a guest is sealed, identical on all three Studios. The phone, not Studio, decides whether a restart needs an approval: the key the phone leaves at its first approval can be missing (on Windows 2026-10-18 a restart still asked the phone while Studio said 'Nothing to approve'), so no line promises that nobody has to act. A sealed first boot never tells the owner to approve before the phone asks (2026-11-02: an install whose late command never ran booted a disk that could not ask, and Studio said 'approve the first unlock on your phone'). The label is 'label'; when the install's last order-status phase shows the box never sealed its key (sealedBootSetUp), the line is notSetUp and the label notSetUpLabel.
awaitingUnlockCopy.stalled: Taking longer than expected — the box may not have reached the network, or it may be waiting for you to approve the unlock on your phone. Check that it's online, or power off and retry.
awaitingUnlockCopy.unlocksOnItsOwn: Unlocking its disk with the key your phone left it. If your phone asks you to approve, approve it there.
awaitingUnlockCopy.firstBoot: Starting. When your phone asks, approve this server's first unlock there. After that it should unlock on its own; if your phone asks again, approve it there.
awaitingUnlockCopy.approveEveryBoot: Starting. When your phone asks, approve the unlock there.
awaitingUnlockCopy.notSetUp: The installer finished, but this server never registered, so there is nothing to approve. Delete it in Studio and create it again from your phone.
awaitingUnlockCopy.label: Starting…

sealedBootSetUp.notes: Whether a sealed guest's first boot can ask for its unlock, judged from the LAST order-status phase seen for its install (fetched once more as the installer stops). The box seals its disk key and reports 'sealing' (then the installer 'installed') before it powers off; an earlier phase means it never registered or sealed, so nothing will ask the phone. null (no serial, or .com unreachable) or an unknown phase keeps the normal copy. Only a server that has never connected is judged.

qemuFailure.notes: Plain failure text for a hosted VM's QEMU (Windows and Linux Studio; the Mac's Virtualization.framework errors are already plain). Studio checks free RAM before launching (checkFree: need = the VM's memory, headroom per host OS, null = enough, otherwise the message) and, when QEMU still dies, shows the memory sentence for an out-of-memory failure (WHPX 'failed to map GPA range', 'Cannot allocate memory') and otherwise only the LAST meaningful stderr line: blank lines and 'warning:' lines (the repeated host-CPUID feature warnings) are dropped and the 'qemu-system-x86_64(.exe): ' program prefix is stripped. Windows 2026-10-18 showed the raw stderr in the sidebar when a second 4 GiB VM started with under 5 GB free.

artifactPreflight.notes: Before Studio makes anything (no VM, no remastered ISO, no USB write) it checks that the signed box release the install will download exists: the bootstrap (SEC-INSTALL-001, packages/flagship-builder/src/userdata.ts) fetches <control host>/build/iso/flagship-box-<first 12 of the recipe's installerGitRef>-<arch>.{tar.gz,manifest.json} and stops for good when it is missing (2026-11-02: home.serene-parrot, a 0.3 recipe against a control plane that did not publish 0.3 yet). Studio sends one HEAD for the manifest with a short timeout. The control host is the one Studio already follows (FLAGSHIP_CONTROL_HOST, else flagshipserver.com; the gym publishes at gym.flagshipserver.com/build/iso). arch is the guest's: amd64 for a USB burn or a saved ISO, the host's for Host here. A recipe whose installerGitRef is not an exact 40-character lowercase commit, or an arch that is neither amd64 nor arm64, has no URL (url null) and is 'missing' without a request: the bootstrap would refuse it too. Verdicts: a 2xx is 'published'; 404 and 410 are 'missing' (refuse with messages.missing); any other status, a timeout or a network failure is 'unreachable' (refuse with messages.unreachable, which asks to try again). Host here from a prebuilt appliance built for the recipe's commit needs no check: the release is already on its disk and the bootstrap downloads nothing (FLAGSHIP_APPLIANCE_PREINSTALLED). Each Studio shows the messages in the owner's language from its i18n catalog; these are the English.

olderAppRecipe.notes: A recipe made by a Flagship app older than 0.3 (its signed install blob names installerGitRef 'main', a tag or nothing at all, never an exact commit) can't install: the bootstrap refuses any installerGitRef that is not an exact 40-character lowercase commit, because a branch or tag can move after the recipe is signed. Studio (Mac, Windows, Linux) and the phone's own USB burn (Android) check this when the recipe is loaded, after its signature verifies, and refuse with the message below, creating nothing (no VM, no ISO, no USB write); the owner rule (F9) is that an old client or recipe leads to a clear 'update' sentence, never a technical refusal. The rule: trim surrounding whitespace (the bootstrap does), then the ref must match ^[0-9a-f]{40}$; anything else, an absent ref (null) included, is from an older app. Each port shows the message in the owner's language from its i18n catalog; 'studio' is the English Studio text, 'phone' the English Android text (the phone that burns is the one to update).
